subject: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)
body:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

Team — consolidating the beta feedback we’ve gotten so far (support tickets + cohort check-ins + SE notes) and a proposal for phase-2 scope. Goal here is to keep momentum while addressing the trust blockers that are slowing adoption.

Summary: what we’re hearing (themes)

1) Trust + explainability ("Do I believe this number?")
- Customers want to understand *basis of estimate* (time window, baseline, token metering source, assumptions).
- “Estimated savings” is fine, but the UI needs a clearer why/why-not and a quick way to sanity check.
- Support tickets mention week-over-week changes feel random without context. (SUP-19344)

2) Confidence vs Risk confusion
- “High risk” is interpreted as “don’t do it” even when it’s just uncertainty / workload variance.
- Conversely, some low-risk suggestions still get questioned because confidence in the savings estimate isn’t explicit.
- Multiple asks to either show confidence separately OR clarify that risk is about potential regression + reversibility. (SUP-19402)

3) Missing suggestions / empty state frustration
- “No suggestions” reads as “product isn’t working,” not “we don’t have enough telemetry.”
- We have at least one known bug case where there *is* traffic but baselines are stale/missing. (SUP-19361; ties to telemetry freshness)
- People want a troubleshooting path: what telemetry is required, what threshold is needed, when it will populate.

4) Strong pull for “apply”
- Most cohort users asked for 1-click apply (or at least “apply draft”) and an audit trail.
- BUT they also want guardrails: rollback, preview, and a way to scope changes (route/model/region).

What’s working (keep)
- The list + detail drawer flow is landing.
- The rationale bullets in the drawer materially reduced “vague” feedback.
- Read-only beta is appropriate for now; it helped us catch telemetry/risk messaging issues without causing regressions.

Phase-2 proposal (recommended)

A) “Apply workflow” (guardrailed, not fully automated)
- Add “Create change” CTA that generates a proposed config diff (batching/caching parameters) with:
  - Preview of before/after settings
  - Scope selection (route/model/region where allowed)
  - Safety checks (SLO headroom, existing rollouts, conflicting settings)
  - Rollback plan (one-click revert to prior config snapshot)
  - Audit log entries and “who approved/applied”
- Rollout mode: canary first (optional) with a default conservative ramp (e.g., 5% → 25% → 100%) in Hosted; Dedicated/Private may need a more explicit approval/ops step.

B) Better explanations + “basis of estimate” improvements
- Show in drawer:
  - Baseline window (e.g., last 7d) and last telemetry refresh timestamp
  - What was measured (tokens in/out, p95 latency, cache hit-rate estimate)
  - Assumptions (e.g., stable prompt prefix, batching compatibility)
  - “Why estimate changed” callout when deltas are driven by traffic mix change or baseline window shift
- Add an “Export details” link (copy JSON) for platform teams to review internally.

C) Confidence surfaced explicitly (paired with risk taxonomy)
- Keep risk as “regression risk” (latency/quality/SLO + reversibility) but add a separate “confidence in savings estimate” indicator.
- This maps to what customers are effectively asking: “Is this safe?” vs “Is this real?”
- We should align with ADR-0274/0275 and avoid creating a third, ambiguous number.

D) “No suggestions” troubleshooting
- Replace empty state with guided checks:
  - Telemetry coverage present?
  - Freshness OK?
  - Minimum traffic threshold met?
  - RBAC permissions ok?
- Include “Last telemetry received” timestamp + link to docs.

E) Measurement: estimated vs realized savings
- For applied suggestions only (phase-2), track realized savings with a simple before/after baseline using consistent windows.
- Record “adopted” event tied to suggestion_id + config change id.

Open questions (need quick alignment)
1) Do we surface confidence as a 3-level label (Low/Med/High) or numeric (0–1)? My read: label is safer and less contentious.
2) Apply workflow: do we require an explicit human approval step for enterprise tenants by default?
3) How strict do we want to be on telemetry freshness before showing savings? (block vs warn)

If folks agree, I’ll draft the phase-2 PRD addendum and we can scope an 8–10 week follow-on, or a smaller 4–6 week “apply-lite + explanations” first increment.

Thanks,
Aditya
—
Aditya Rao
Product Lead, Redwood Optimize
Redwood Inference


From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 10:04 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

+1 on splitting “risk” and “confidence.” The current risk chip is doing too much work.

For apply: I’d like to structure it as “create a rollout” (even if it’s a very simple one) so it matches Console mental models. That also gives us a natural home for rollback + audit trail.

On empty state: we should show *why* there’s nothing (telemetry/freshness/traffic) AND provide a “request help” path for enterprise (routes to CSM/Support).

Happy to co-own PRD addendum with you.

Marissa


From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 11:27 AM PST
Subject: Re: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

Engineering POV:

- Apply-lite is doable if we treat it as generating a config patch that goes through existing control plane APIs (w/ a feature-flag + allowlist).
- We should avoid “true one-click apply” until we have:
  1) schema stability on savings/risk payloads
  2) E2E tests for rollback + permissions
  3) guardrails integrated (auto-disable criteria)

Confidence indicator: +1 for 3-level label. Numeric will create bikeshedding and people will interpret it as a guarantee.

Telemetry freshness gating: I recommend warn-not-block for list view (so page isn’t empty), but block savings $ numbers and show “insufficiently fresh data” inline. Otherwise we’ll keep getting “it disappeared” confusion.

If we agree on “create rollout” concept, I’ll sync with Chloe on where this should live in the BFF / permissions checks.

Dylan


From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 1:09 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

Re: missing suggestions / SUP-19361

We’ve confirmed at least one path where route-level baselines don’t get computed if the tenant’s traffic is split across regions and one region drops below the min threshold during the aggregation window. Net effect: UI says “insufficient telemetry” even though they have traffic.

We can fix with:
- better aggregation fallback (combine regions if per-region is too sparse)
- surfacing “what data is missing” (e.g., tokens_in missing for route X in region Y)
- writing last successful compute time into the payload so the UI can show it

If product wants a hard freshness bar, propose:
- show savings if baseline_age_hours <= 24
- show range + warning if 24 < baseline_age_hours <= 72
- hide $ savings if >72

This should cut down on “week to week” confusion too once the UI shows the baseline window + refresh time.

Logan


From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe_martin@redwoodinference.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Talia Benson <talia_benson@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 2:46 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

Agree on separating risk vs confidence.

Proposed definitions to keep us consistent:
- Risk (Low/Med/High): probability + impact of negative change (latency/quality/SLO), including reversibility.
- Confidence (Low/Med/High): stability/identifiability of savings estimate given telemetry coverage, traffic variance, and model fit quality.

We can reuse pieces of current risk features for confidence (variance, sample size) but keep the user language distinct.

For apply: any “High risk” suggestion should require canary + explicit acknowledgment (“this may increase latency p95 / reduce headroom”).

I can help write the user-facing text to avoid overpromising (“confidence is not a guarantee” etc.).

Jonas

Date: Fri, Feb 20, 2026 at 4:38 PM PST
Subject: Re: Beta feedback summary + phase-2 proposal (Console > Optimize Suggestions)

Thanks all — aligned on direction.

Next steps (I’ll own driving):

1) Phase-2 PRD addendum by Wed EOD
- Scope: apply-lite (create rollout w/ preview + rollback) + basis-of-estimate + confidence label + improved empty state.
- Non-goal (for this increment): fully automated apply without review.

2) Proposed initial sequencing
- Week 1–2: definitions + UI design updates (risk vs confidence copy), data contract updates (telemetry timestamps, baseline windows)
- Week 3–5: apply-lite plumbing + permissions/audit + basic canary support
- Week 6: QA + runbooks + support enablement update

3) Owners (tentative)
- Apply-lite UX + IA: Marissa (with Kenji/Alicia via normal process)
- BFF + permissions + audit: Dylan/Chloe
- Telemetry freshness + baseline fields: Logan (with Nadia/Mei as needed)
- Risk/confidence taxonomy alignment + copy review: Jonas/Karthik
- Support FAQ updates and escalation paths: Dev + Jasmine/Rachel

I’ll include specific asks/decisions in the PRD draft (freshness thresholds + enterprise approval default).

Have a good weekend,
Aditya
